Doubling $N$ reduces cross-seed $\sigma$ by 32\% on NER and 24\% on RE (Table~\ref{tab:sigma-comparison}), with the largest reductions for SJ ($-43\%$ NER) and EM ($-59\%$ NER); additional samples stabilize structural signals more than LP.

\paragraph{$N$-scaling: selection headroom vs.\ selection gain.}
Table~\ref{tab:n_scaling_selection} traces the effect of sample count on degeneracy, oracle headroom, and per-signal selection gain.
Oracle headroom grows roughly linearly with $N$ ($+4.4$~pp at $N{=}2$ to $+20.0$~pp at $N{=}32$).
LP selection improves monotonically with $N$ ($+0.39$~pp at $N{=}8$ to $+0.95$~pp at $N{=}32$), but even at $N{=}32$, where degeneracy falls to 4\% and oracle headroom reaches ${\sim}20$~pp, the best signal captures less than 5\% of the available improvement.
Degeneracy drops monotonically (43\% at $N{=}2$ to 4\% at $N{=}32$), yet reduced degeneracy does not unlock selection, consistent with the LoRA-rank ablation finding (\S\ref{sec:robustness_main}).
VC selection degrades with increasing $N$ ($-2.66$~pp at $N{=}2$ to $-4.35$~pp at $N{=}32$), consistent with mode-seeking bias in voting-based selection as the candidate pool grows.

\paragraph{Non-tied subset and $N$-scaling.}
Where compression is mitigated (LP range ${\geq}0.05$, $n{=}210$), within-instance $\rho$ rises to 0.39 and LP selection yields $+2.9$~pp ($p{=}0.004$, survives Bonferroni; Table~\ref{tab:nontied_main}).
LP scales with $N$ in the low-degeneracy regime ($+0.52$~pp from $N{=}8$ to 16 on Few-NERD, $p{=}0.003$; \S\ref{sec:fewnerd}); on SciERC, even $N{=}32$ captures less than 5\% of headroom (Table~\ref{tab:n_scaling_selection}).
An oracle tiebreaker within VC-equivalent groups recovers $+7.9$~pp, confirming per-sample signal exists but current signals cannot extract it (full analyses in Appendices~\ref{app:n_scaling}, \ref{app:verbalized_confidence}, \ref{app:vc_quartile}).

\paragraph{LP compression mechanisms.}
Four non-mutually-exclusive mechanisms contribute: token-level averaging, schema-dominated tokens, vocabulary restriction under constrained decoding, and format-token dilution.
Free-form decoding rules out constraint-imposed mechanisms for NER (std ratio 0.97; Appendix~\ref{app:freeform_ablation}) but restores LP selection for RE ($+2.35$~pp, $p{=}0.025$; Appendix~\ref{app:re_extension}).

**Positive contribution (A)**: Confidence signals reliably predict structured IE output quality at the population level (AUROC up to 0.82, ρ up to 0.45), enabling practical QE/selective prediction.
**Diagnostic contribution (B)**: Selection effectiveness requires TWO conditions (D123):
- **Condition 1 — Low degeneracy**: High degeneracy eliminates headroom (CoNLL 47.4% degen → 0 net selection gain regardless of signal). Unified definition: Constant F1, gold-filtered.

The framing is NOT "selection fails" (pure negative) but "we show WHEN it works (LP in low-degeneracy), WHY it fails elsewhere (degeneracy + compression), and WHAT distinguishes LP from structural signals" (diagnostic with constructive implications).

- Layer A (design property, noted not discovered): 4/5 signals are instance-level aggregates → cannot rank candidates by construction. This is a conceptual clarification — the "methodological premise" — not an empirical finding.
